title: Enumerable: choose the shape of the result
outcome: Use each, map, select, find, and reduce without hiding side effects.
cue: Map changes shape inside. Select changes who stays.

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A developer writes tasks.map { |t| t if t[:done] }. They expect only done tasks. What does the result actually contain? Repair it.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: You need the first overdue task among a million database rows. Why might to_a.find be a bad first choice?

trace.title: Collection
trace.detail: A block is a chunk of behavior passed to a method. Enumerable gives collections common operations. Choose by the result you need: each for an action, map for one output per input, select for a subset, find for one match, and reduce for an accumulated result.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
For map, write the block result below each input. For select, write keep/drop below each input. For reduce, write the accumulator after each step.

yield calls the provided block. A method that may be called without one can check block_given?. An Enumerator can defer iteration. lazy can avoid creating intermediate arrays, but the work still happens when a terminal operation asks for results.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: Using map only to send messages communicates the wrong intent and allocates an unused array. A query followed by Ruby select can load far more database rows than a SQL where clause.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Use each, map, select, find, and reduce without hiding side effects. Give a concrete failure example.
